*External Shell: This bug's body is soft and vulnerable, but they have an external shell into which they may retreat for safety. If they do, they may attempt a Soak roll against the damage. Bugs with an Absorption score or external shell that has an Absorption score may use that value in place of Shell on the roll.

When the Initiate would cast a Spell with a range of Touch or farther, they may cast that Spell through a weapon. When making their attack roll, dice equal to the Soul spent on the Spell are added to the roll. If the attack hits, the target is damaged by the weapon and affected by the Spell.

разумные-16.name: Cicada Saboteur
разумные-16.text:
Cicada Saboteurs are often “planted” somewhere and left to hibernate until they detect unexpected activity. Once roused, they spring to action and begin elaborate tunnel networks, used for guerilla warfare, spying, and gathering corpses to turn into husks.  
*“Sleeper agents, in the literal sense of the word.”*  
Size: _ / Mi _ / In _ / Sh _ / Gr _ / Heart _ / Soul _ / Stamina _  
Speed: _ / Spook: 1 / Cute: 1 / Hunger: _  
   
Tunneling: This bug can burrow through soil at a rate of 1 square for 2 Speed. It may choose to leave a tunnel behind, or not. If the bug is underground with no source of air, it will suffer Suffocation.  
Hibernation: With this trait, a bug can stay still or sedentary for extended periods of time without running out of oxygen or food. While Hibernating, a bug cannot suffocate and its Belly consumed per rest is reduced to 5. However, a Hibernating bug suffers a -2 penalty to notice things happening around it unless directly interacted with, and loses its first turn if woken abruptly.  
Song (Haunting): This bug is capable of creating a distinctive song, capable of being heard over long distances. If soothing, the user treats its Cute as 1 higher in interactions with bugs who have heard its song. If haunting, the user treats its Spook as 1 higher instead. Songs created by this trait are known to sometimes attract the attention of spirits.  
Rank 1 - Dust Initiate  
*The Hollowing*  
The Initiate of Dust may never take Ranks in Bloom. The Initiate may perform a ritual costing 2 Soul upon any corpse that does not have a Soft Body, hollowing it out and filling it with sand and dust. The ritual takes 1 hour, and transforms the corpse into a Husk.  
*Army of Dust*  
The Initiate can control a number of husks equal to their Dust Rank, and they act after the Initiate’s initiative. Any Husks in excess of the creator’s Rank in Dust cost 2 Notches as well. Releasing a Husk from control may be done freely, and returns it to a mundane corpse. If its creator dies, the Husk becomes uncontrolled, and it will attempt to attack and eat any creature that does not have the Barren Trait or Ranks in Dust.

Equipment: Camouflage cloak (+1 Stealth reroll), Light Talisman (Worn on body, \+1 reroll on resistance checks against magic), Digging tools

=Husks=

A Husk is created when a bug’s corpse is animated by a powerful curse or infection.  
When a bug becomes a Husk, it loses the following:

* All Arts, Arcanas and Recipes  
* All Notches  
* All Techniques  
* All Hearts  
* All Paths  
* All Proficiencies  
* All former knowledge and memories  
* The ability to speak

Its statistics change in the subsequent ways:

* It loses 2 Speed (to a minimum of 1)  
* It gains 2 Spook and loses 2 Cute  
* Its Insight becomes 0  
* Its Stamina becomes 3  
* Its Soul becomes 2 (generally the same Soul spent to animate it)  
* It gains Absorption 10

It keeps the same Traits it had in life (except Mental traits) and interacts with existing rules in different ways, as described here.  
Heart and damage: A Husk no longer has a Heart pool. It uses Shell in place of Heart.  
Death and re-raising: When the Husk’s Shell reaches 0, the Husk collapses and is considered to have died. It may be raised again later unless its Shell is permanently reduced to 0, smashing the Husk to dust. If raised again, it keeps any permanent Shell damage it already had.  
Mindless: A Husk is considered an object for the purposes of Dream and Nightmare magic. It is immune to Morale, Stress, fear and mind-affecting magic.
=Dust Husks=

*Their Lord decreed, and the dead rose to serve once again. “Rise, hunger, and fall. For Dust you are, and unto Dust you shall return.”*

Dust Husks are types of Husks raised by necromancers loyal to the Dustwyrm. They may be encountered as minions under a necromancer’s control, or as rogue, autonomous, mindless machines of decay.

They interact with existing rules in different ways, as described here.  
Regaining Soul: A Dust Husk’s Soul may only be replenished by the Husk’s creator touching it and Focusing Soul into it.  
Regaining Shell: A Husk cannot regain Shell unless the Shell damage suffered was temporary (for example, from a hook weapon’s strike).  
Running out of Soul: A Dust Husk with 0 Soul becomes a mundane corpse once more. It may be raised again later.  
Flasks, Drugs, Poisons, Food, etc.: A Dust Husk experiences no benefit or harm from organic substances. (It is still affected by substances such as acid, even from an organic source.)  
Bleeding: A Dust Husk has no blood. It is still affected by bleeding, losing sand and dust in place of blood.  
Hunger. Dust Husks have no Hunger, but rogue ones may still eat mindlessly.

*“Flavor text”*

A sect of Oakwyrm worshipers, the Cult of the Gibbets is composed primarily of wasps, with rare mantid members. They act under Overseer Danika’s command as the executioners of the Kingdom’s most vile criminals, traitors and monsters.  
In its pursuit of power, fueled by the desire to destroy the Oakwyrm's enemies at any cost, the Cult has harnessed a twisted echo of the God-Tree’s essence, one that has infused the Gibbets region ever since the Lord of Dust himself visited its branches aeons ago. Members of the Cult make prominent use of this dreadful new magic, and some know the following unique Arcana.

разумные-42.name: Cult of the Gibbets Arcana
разумные-42.text:
Paladin's Brand  
Difficulty: 2 ---- Range: Touch ---- Duration: Brief  
The caster chooses a weapon it wields. It flares with burning arcane light, dealing 1 extra magical damage with the caster’s attacks or arts. If it kills an enemy, the caster regains 1 Heart.  
Enemies adjacent to the caster that have the Darkvision trait, the Barren trait, or ranks in Paths of foul magic (such as Dust, Nightmare or Thorn) also have -1 to attack and defense rolls.

Absorb  
Difficulty: 1 ---- Range: Touch  
The caster latches onto a target and steals its life force to refill their own. Deals 2 damage to the target and restores 1 Heart to the caster. If the target dies, the caster regains 1 Soul. When enhancing this Arcana, Hearts regained cannot exceed the damage dealt.*

Warding Wall  
Difficulty: 2 ---- Range: Self ---- Duration: Brief  
A wall of pulsating, sickly yellow light extends horizontally from the caster’s body.  
The wall contains the caster at its very center, and is 2 spaces tall, 2 spaces thick and 5 spaces wide.  
The wall blocks any physical attack coming from the outside, including projectiles and reach weapons.  
Enemies that attempt to walk across the wall must contest Shell against a free touch spell attack roll by the caster. On a failure, they lose 2 Stamina per space travelled through the wall.  
Allies inside the wall recieve \+4 to soak rolls against all damage sources. This includes the caster.  
If the caster attacks, moves or is moved, the wall dissipates.

Gall Paladin

The Cult of the Gibbets executes criminals in a brutal fashion, impaling them on the twisted, deathly-sharp branches that grow in their home region. These branches serve another purpose, however: wasp larva buried underneath can then feed on the slain prisoners’ life force, soaked up by tumorous galls in the bark. These “gall wasps” grow, learn and mature at an accelerated pace, and display increased strength and often massive size compared to the average for their species. This allows Overseer Danika to fill her ranks with battle-ready soldiers at a rapid rate. Paladins bearing the Gibbets Crest are fiercely loyal and obedient, but as their appearance inspires disgust and distrust, they are seldom seen beyond Overseer Danika’s territory.  
Thus far, no attempts at performing the ritual on other species’ larvae have been made.  
The blood and flesh of these wasps is toxic to other creatures, and burns like acid to the touch.

дикие-17.name: Tramapodes
дикие-17.text:
Are long, many-legged bugs of burden used to transport travelers and merchandise alike. They contort effortlessly through the God-Tree's web of twisting, termite-dug tunnels, and their wave-shaped, scaled back is fit to carry dozens of passengers at a time. While Tramapodes are docile, obedient and far from mindless, they are slow to process information. In extreme cases, an individual may bumble in and out of danger without even realizing it.  
The glowing beady eyes hidden within the darkness of their cowl-like face-plates are specialized for underground travel, but do not fare well under sunlight. In spite of this, they are sometimes requisitioned for military purposes. Such a decision is not made lightly, as it can paralyze trade throughout the God-Tree for the duration of an entire Chorus.

*“Oh, they’re controversial alright. But let me tell you, it’s not their slow wit or whether they belong on the battlefield that gets people’s antennas in a twist. It’s the name. Me, I don’t know what a ‘tram’ is and I don’t care.” -Mani, Tramapode handler*

Mi 8 (Load 16) / Gr 1 / In 2 / Sh 5  
Heart 20 / Stamina 5 / Soul 3  
Speed 7 / Cute 2 / Spook 1 / Hunger: 30  
Traits: Feral, Herbivore, Extra Legs (Polypod), Contortionist (Unfold), Darkvision, Nearsighted  
Special: An unalerted Tramapode does not react to the events of a Scene until the Scene ends. If properly communicated with, or given significant stimuli (pain, blinding light, great noise...), a Tramapode enters a mildly alert state until the end of the Scene. Any action a mildly alert Tramapode takes is a Focus action, taking place when the focus resolves.

stats.traits: Feral, Herbivore, Extra Legs (Polypod), Contortionist (Unfold), Darkvision, Nearsighted

дикие-18.name: Barkbite
дикие-18.text:
A common pet in Oakshade. Wags its stinger when excited. They can use their mandibles for peeling up bark, which wild ones use to dig up burrowing prey. Nobility has recently taken to breeding for cuteness, at the cost of intelligence. These ‘noble-bred’ are not often found beyond the tree itself.

*“Bug’s best friend! Or so they say anyway. The Bark is certainly lesser to its Bite, which makes them good guard and patrol creatures.”*

дикие-19.name: Lightningbugs
дикие-19.text:
Curious creatures originating from the Scorched City of Barkhearth. Small and unassuming, save for their abdomens, which crackle fiercely with electricity. Lightningbugs are not aggressive, but tend to be territorial and easily angered. 

*“The strangest thing - the species never existed before lightning struck that city. Where did they come from?”*

 Heart 3 / Soul 3 / Stamina 3  
Speed: 7 / Cute: 1,5 / Hunger: 5  
Traits: Armless, Flight, Feral

Striking a lightningbug with a metal-based melee weapon causes 1 damage to the attacker.  
Difficulty Rating: 1  
\

дикие-20.name: Statiks
дикие-20.text:
A subspecies of tiktiks that appears to have survived the destruction of Barkhearth. As with others of the species, they wander the area aimlessly in search of scraps left be larger predators and foragers. However, between the tiktiks is a charged beam of energy that shocks anyone it passes through.

*“Whether their strange traits are what facilitated their survival, or are a result of it, remains unclear*.*”*

Special: Charged Tiktiks create a line between themselves and nearby lightningbugs. Any bug entering this line, or that the line crosses paths with, takes 1 damage. Any lightningbugs that pass between two charged tiktiks regain 1 Soul.  
Difficulty Rating: 0

дикие-21.name: Roundscales
дикие-21.text:
Large, rotund bugs with gleaming pearlescent shells. They are typically docile, but have a habit of taking naps in the middle of well travelled tunnels within and beneath the tree. If threatened, they will curl up and roll over their assailants. Their pearly shells are often sought after, but they are considered to be a protected species, as a certain wealthy wasp likes to keep them as pets.

*“Bestiary Quote”*

Heart 6 / Soul 2 / Stamina 3

дикие-22.name: Palnails
дикие-22.text:
Are a friendly mollusc species that have been tamed and domesticated by Oakshadians over generations. They have legs uncharacteristic of other members of their kind, and are able to reach surprising speeds when rolling in their magic resistant shells.

дикие-23.name: Taptiks
дикие-23.text:
Tiny critters which use their specialized proboscises to draw water from the tree, or tap into underground water sources. Often they are kept or captured by travelers to tap water, by slicing off their head and using it as a tap.

*“Sometimes I wonder how travelers can bear to lop the head off of such a helpless little thing. But I’ve seen in my travels what hunger and thirst can do to a bug.”*

Difficulty Rating: 0

stats.traits: Sharp Proboscis, Armless, Climbing, Spiky, Itsy Bitsy, Feral

дикие-24.name: Mosslings
дикие-24.text:
Sapient creatures born from the eponymous Mossgrove, a lush hollow in the side of the God-Tree. Certain genus can also be found in farther away places, with matching vegetation colors.

*“Curious creatures, these ones. They certainly possess some form of intelligence despite their simple living. Appearing to survive out of the sheer humidity in the air. Don’t let the cutesy look fool you, a mossling is capable of great spontaneous magic!”

дикие-29.text:
Aggressive cave dwelling creatures. They tend to gather in underground hives where they return to feed their young.

*“The end of many an unprepared explorer. They're nasty, erratic critters but kill enough of them and the rest should scatter away. They dwell in tight packs under great bark hovels or even cave systems.”*

Hardy cave-dwelling beasts which often steal food from travelers within the Oakshade area. Though not aggressive, they will attack if confronted or provoked.

дикие-31.name: Springtails
дикие-31.description: a species of bugs with large, powerful tails that allow them to spring from place to place in the grass canopy. Specimens have been kept in captivity underground by ants, and farmed for their large tails, which gradually grow back when detached. For their size, they have impressive physical strength.

дикие-32.description: large and lumbering but rather dim underground creatures. The back of their shells tend to resemble surface crystals. Not to be underestimated.

дикие-33.name: Aestid
дикие-33.text:
A species of skulking bugs, thin and skeletal in appearance. The Aestid’s rubbery outer shell secretes a fluid which prevents the dust from digging into its flesh. The fluid contains sensitive ‘eyespots’ which detect smells, using this to communicate and navigate. Aestids are scavengers, and do not adhere to a pack structure, though they may work together to take down live prey if hungry enough.

*“Possibly related to Strugers. These enduring beasts have long since adapted to survive beneath the terror wings of the Lord of Dust... Let us hope we will never need to.”*

Heart 8 / Soul 1 / Stamina 4

дикие-34.name: Sniffid
дикие-34.text:
A flying bug mysteriously untouched by the storms above the moor. Looked upon as an omen of disaster and misfortune by most, or an omen of favor by followers of the Dust. Its scaled wings and stingers share the faded red color of the land’s soil.

*“Refugees seeking asylum from the lands of the Dust have told me never to linger under the eyes of a Sniffid. It is a commonly held superstition that the Lord of Dust can see through their eyes.”*

stats.traits: Flight, Airborne, Armless, Legless, Sharp Proboscis, Stinger, Barren, Feral

дикие-35.name: Lord-Barrens
дикие-35.text:
Horrific dead-eyed abominations which lurk beneath the dusted badlands. They sit just below the surface, then rise up to devour anything nearby. Sometimes they are sent to the frontlines of the horde as siege weapons, burrowing under fortifications or into ant nests. Each lord-barren is controlled directly by the Sandwyrm, acting as his avatars to lead his army, for his presence would turn even his own followers to dust.

*“Many of the border fortresses hold out against the horde, until its Lord grows tired of waiting and sends one or two of those monstrosities to bring it down. I’ve heard there is one above all the others, the Sandwyrm’s own prized son, a prince of destruction.”*

Size: Great+ (6x6) / Mi: 8 / In - / Absorption 6 / Gr 2  
 Heart 25 / Soul 3 / Stamina 7  
Speed: 5 / Spook: 4.5 / Hunger: 45

Special II: Sandstorm. Lord-barrens are accompanied by a small sandstorm with a 10 square radius which is treated as difficult terrain for flying bugs, causing them to lose 5 squares of altitude at the end of each turn. Creatures within the sandstorm suffer a -1 penalty to accuracy checks.  
Special III: Devour. A lord-barren that slays a creature grappled by its mandibles may Devour it immediately. It may also make a second grapple check against a creature grappled by its mandibles to attempt to Devour it alive. Creatures devoured alive suffer the effects of the lord-barren’s Natural Projectile at the end of each of their turns, but may damage it from the inside, ignoring Absorption.  
Absorption gained through Devour may exceed a lord-barren’s base Absorption score, up to a cap of 10.

дикие-36.name: Deathrowers
дикие-36.description: small scurrying critters that lurk under rocks in the moor. They vomit stomach acid on passersby, then scurry away and wait for them to leave, before returning to suck up the liquefied flesh that sloughs off. Cowards by nature, deathrowers will avoid confrontation at all costs.

дикие-37.name: Dust Devils

When something stands between the Dust Devil and its goal, it unleashes its secret weapon : a miniature sandstorm of its own.

дикие-39.name: Beadfly

дикие-40.description: a large flying bug which makes its nest by tying together blades of tall grass. дикие-41.name: Green Terroraptors
дикие-41.description: the apex predators of the more shrouded wealds. Terroraptors are well tailored killing machines, with enough natural armaments and physique that even veteran hunters do not dare take on them unprepared. They tend to not venture too close to civilization and have both hides and claws that fetch extremely good prices in the right markets.

дикие-42.name: Dragonflies
дикие-42.description: also known as lesser wyrms, are huge bugs capable of flying at terrifying speeds. Spans of land that would take a bug weeks to traverse take mere hours to these beasts. When they wish to catch food, they spew lightning from their mandibles, and feast on the charred corpses. Their young larvae grow in the bayou’s waters, and so that region is where they nest.
дикие-42.text:
“The dragonflies hunt everywhere, but not the lands of the Dust - perhaps thinking it the territory of an old and terrible kin.”*

дикие-43.description: timid, graceful swimmers that populate the Bayou’s dirty waters. They sing to attract Lifeblood Seeds, which they feed upon. Rarely, a tamed Murkloon can be observed pulling crafts along the water.

Special II - Heretic Beast: The Archloon’s Hearts are all Lifeblood Hearts. It may focus to heal Lifeblood Hearts, up to its base Lifeblood Heart count.  
Special III - Siphon (costs 1 Lifeblood, 1/turn): The Archloon contests Shell with a bug it touches, with \+2 to its roll. If the target fails, the Archloon siphons their blood into its own body, converting it to lifeblood: the target suffers 2 unsoakable damage and the  Archloon gains 2 Lifeblood Hearts (+1 per Lifeblood Heart the target lost, and an extra \+2 if this damage kills the target).  
Special IV - Lifeburn (1/turn, replaces a use of Siphon): The Archloon may spend up to 4 Lifeblood Hearts as Stamina for a single action. May be also activated as part of or to initiate a Parry, Dodge, or Attack of Opportunity.  
Special V - Reorigination (costs 1 Lifeblood, 1/turn, replaces a use of Siphon): The Archloon consumes the lifeblood within its body, healing all Attribute damage and cleansing 2 points from a DoT affecting it. For 1 more Lifeblood, this ability may be used on a target the Archloon can touch.
*Variant:* Archloons may swap prepared Arts for Stunning Strike, Stag Throw, or Garrote.

stats.traits: Luminous, Armless, Legless, Feral, Swimming (Waterbreathing), Contortionist (Unfold), Blood of the Ancients (Primal Ichor), Slam, Song (Soothing)

дикие-45.name: Rotchurns
дикие-45.description: tiny, voracious carrion feeders that swarm any dead matter that falls into the water. They are known to reflexively attack creatures that come too close to one of their ongoing feeding frenzies.

дикие-46.name: Kookitos
дикие-46.description: a species of beach-dwelling critters which hide beneath the sand to ambush unwary prey, flipping them over with the top of their shell. The inside of a kookitos is soft and juicy, and they are often hunted for their meat. They store melted sand in a special sac within their gut, mixed with stomach acids into a sticky mixture that beachside villages sometimes extract to use as mortar.
дикие-46.text:
“I have taken to carrying a staff with me when I walk the Still Coast, tapping it in front of my feet as though I were blind.”*

дикие-47.name: Squirts
дикие-47.description: aquatic bugs with a gland that produces thick black ink, with which they blind would-be predators in order to escape. Flocks of squirts are tended to by Sourcepool-aligned settlements along the south coast of the Stillwater Sea, where their ink is harvested for use in writing.
дикие-47.text:
“It’s one thing to walk like a blind bug, but actually going blind... I’ll be keeping this staff.”*

дикие-48.name: Ridgebacks
дикие-48.description: livestock kept by the shore-dwellers to harvest their blood for its health benefits. The ridgebacks are generally quite happy to be kept, so long as they are kept fed. A starving ridgeback can be terrifying, as they vomit shell-dissolving foam.
дикие-48.text:
“I used to hear this crab captain talk constantly about a ‘big white one’ he swore he would hook one day. I can scarcely imagine a larger one of these things.”*

дикие-49.name: Lotus Skimmer
дикие-49.description: a species camouflaged as a flowering plant that floats on top of the water. They filter feed to survive and are practically harmless, and so civilized bugs often tame them for use as water transport. They have weak wings that allow them to make brief hops, or act as paddles in the water.
дикие-49.text:
“They’re just as fast and enduring as your average raft, more flexible… and compared to a hunk of rope and shellwood, they make for far better company.*  
*I’m told some can grow to impressive sizes, but I’ve yet to see it with my own eyes.”*

дикие-50.name: Glulbs
дикие-50.description: a species of intelligent predators that lurk at sea, drawing in sailors with their glowing heads beneath the water. Once a vessel or diver draws close enough, they climb aboard to claim their meal. Although their colorful lightshows are beautiful, the glulbs themselves are hideous to behold.

дикие-51.name: Bogleeches
дикие-51.description: commonly found in and around fetid swamp-waters. These fiends are mindlessly aggressive if their strong sense of smell picks up the scent of blood or guts.
дикие-51.text:
“Be wary of disposing of corpses or waste near river waters. Leeches are quickly drawn around and a single infected bite might do you in.”*

дикие-52.name: Rotguts
дикие-52.description: membranous creatures which swim leisurely through the still water. Their tendrils pack a nasty sting, which they use to incapacitate and kill prey by draining their fluids. The fluid inside of them is alcoholic, and they are sometimes harvested by sailors on the one sea to raise morale. A dangerous prospect, as they are living depth charges.
дикие-52.text:
“We’re stuck in the doldrums for the time being, and fresh gutbrew was a welcome distraction, even if we had to patch up a chunk of the hull. I dread the day someone figures out how to use these things for naval combat. Or slingapult warfare. Or guerilla actions. In the name of all that is High and Holy, if some drunken shipmate gets the brilliant idea to experiment mid-voyage...”*

Special II: Explosive Retaliation. When a Rotgut is killed by fire or piercing damage, its brewing organ ruptures and explodes, dealing 2 soakable damage to all adjacent creatures unless they make a dodge check with at least 1 success. дикие-53.name: Blots
дикие-53.description: a curious and docile shelled creature found in the deepest caverns, under both root and web. They are very difficult to harm, or even tell where their actual body is*, and sometimes respond to threats with innate abilities resembling Spire and Void. Blots do not seem to eat other bugs and are not aggressive unless provoked, though they can sense magic, and curiously investigate sources of magic, light, and noise. Blots leave an inky trail of liquid void behind them wherever they tread. Most of the liquid forms into puddles and eventually dissipates, but sometimes these puddles begin to move about on their own. Such creatures are called smudges, and are usually short-lived; slowly fading away over the course of a few days.

дикие-54.name: Voidworm
дикие-54.description: a void-based predator that swims through the abyssal sea. Drawn to foreign objects that dare tread the inky waters, it pursues boats and bugs on the surface and drags them into the deep.
дикие-54.text:
“The blackness beneath our ship roiled, what felt like a thousand blazing white eyes looking up at us. Not with hatred, but with unquenchable purpose.”*

дикие-55.name: Shadows
дикие-55.description: seemingly sapient creatures capable of taking on the forms of other sapient bugs. Though many develop individual motives, they all possess a strong desire to kill and replace individuals who garner their interest. Few have ever seen them in their true form, which is much like a spider head with spindly limbs sprouting from it. Infiltrating Shadows are often uncovered among the spiders of Deeproot, who have developed a test: find those whose ichor turns black under daylight, find the Shadows.
дикие-55.text:
“Is it constant infiltration by Shadows that drove the Weavers to what we call paranoid xenophobia? Or were they the only ones smart enough to discover their stalkers?”*  
Size: Average / Mi: 3 / In 3 / Sh - (3) / Gr 3 / Heart 10 / Soul 0 / Stamina 3  
Speed: 6 / Spook: 2 / Hunger: 6  
Traits: Soft Body, Alien Body (Internal), Extra Legs, Devour (Identity), Talent: Deception, Dead Silent  
Special I: Sapient. Shadows are fully sapient and capable of gaining Path Ranks and Proficiencies. Shadows with Mystic Ranks gain max Soul as normal, but do not generate Soul through rest.  
Special II: Steal Form. Shadows can take the form of any bug they see at the cost of 1 Stamina, gaining all of that bug’s Traits and replacing their own, except for Alien Body (Internal), Talent: Deception and Devour (Identity).  
Special III: Absorb Memories. When a Shadow Devours the bug whose form it has stolen, it gains that bug’s Path Ranks, Proficiencies, Arcana, Arts, and memories, overwriting any Path Ranks the Shadow had before. The Shadow also gains a normal Soul pool and the ability to regenerate Soul, and loses Devour (Identity).  
Some Shadows forget what they were and truly believe they are the bug they replaced. Others retain their true nature. Shadows who grow bored of their current life can shed their shape and take the form of another bug. They regain Devour (Identity), but lose all the abilities that they acquired from their previous life.

дикие-56.name: The Kraken
дикие-56.description: a vast entity that lurks in the depths of the Abyssal Sea, reaching up with huge tendrils to drag down ships that earn its ire. The Kraken’s attention is drawn most of all by the use of Essence-based magic.
дикие-56.text: “I have seen one of these appendages but once, and I confess, it bore a striking resemblance to one of the roots I saw hanging above.”

дикие-58.name: Lightdrinkers
дикие-58.description: lumafly-like bugs which float listlessly in the air above the Abyssal Sea. They seek out and suck the light out of any light source in sight. Their wings glow a gentle cyan color.

дикие-59.name: Meridiens
дикие-59.description: a species of floating membraned creatures which feed primarily upon lightdrinkers. They are brilliant and mesmerizing to watch, but harbor a violent jealousy towards other light sources. Sometimes they will even devour newly budded offspring that do not flee quickly enough.

дикие-60.name: Pallbearers
дикие-60.description: creatures that wander the lower caverns and inhabit the landmasses in the abyssal sea. They gather the masks or faces of those they kill, or those who wash up on their shore. Pallbearers gather in what appear to be small community or family units, building shrines from the faces they collect. Although they appear to be bugs at first glance, each pallbearer is in fact a gathering of many long, inky-colored worms coiled and intertwined within a mask, wearing clothes left behind by the fallen. Interestingly, pallbearers appear to craft their own masks, and never use the faces they keep enshrined; yet some are known to wear the bodies of the dead from the ‘neck’ down. A pallbearer is typically not hostile, but they are startled and become violent when exposed to loud noises, and react similarly when their mask shrines are disturbed.
